about: Data of scripts/parity/origin-replay.mjs (iteration 14, step 7): how a replay's result is read and how each difference from the origin is classified. No origin content: no change name, commit, branch or merge request body. A rule matches a difference when every field of its `match` holds; the first matching rule classifies it. An `explained` rule cites a lessons row by a phrase of that row, resolved at run time to docs/lessons/<file>:<line> the way scripts/check-lessons.mjs reads the tables; a citation that resolves to no row makes the difference a defect. A difference no rule matches is a defect when it is strong (D7) and recorded only otherwise.

commitKinds.subject: ^chore\(replay\): |\(the rest of the origin's fix commit\)$

rules.why: The origin plan's tasks outside every group were added at verify and run on the change branch after every group merged; the port records such work against the owning task's Files block, so plan-lint refusing a fresh plan with unassigned tasks is the port's rule (D8; step 8 confirms it on every regular origin plan).
The driver added the origin's unassigned tasks to a group so the port schedules them.

match.what: review\.mjs fix refuses the origin's fix

cite.phrase: touching the finding's file and otherwise only test files, and no other finding's fix

rules.why: The origin's own rule is one fix commit touching only its finding's file; the port checks it, the origin did not. Whether the check should allow a fix's collateral non-test files is the developer's decision.

cite.phrase: every deviation must be cited by a `debt` (forced) or a `ruling` (a judgement), so the read is checked

rules.why: The port checks that every deviation and every recorded or accepted finding is placed; the origin's ledger places deviations and findings nowhere it can check.

cite.phrase: every deviation must be cited by a `debt` (forced) or a `ruling` (a judgement), so the read is checked

rules.why: The ruling citing a deviation is the record the port's placements check requires.

cite.phrase: a recorded finding closes in the ledger too, `resolve --finding F<n>` (a field of the port's own)

rules.why: A port-only record: the port places a recorded or accepted finding in the ledger.
The origin plan names the files by a glob or an unbackticked path its own check read; the port reads only backticked full paths (docs/lessons/verify.md, "Verify reads only a backticked path.").
The origin edited a main spec at or below `## Requirements` by hand in a task commit, which its flow allowed then; the port's c4 fails such an edit, since only archive writes the requirements.
The port lists the origin's hand edit of a main spec as a prose edit the origin's verify did not count; the origin reply does not answer it.
The origin's c4 reply names a prose-edit commit of the origin's verify phase, which the replay never made (D5).

cite.phrase: the core proposes `<type>/<change>`, and `<type>/<KEY>/<change>` when the scope gives a branch key

rules.why: The port proposes a type from the change name's prefix, or asks for one, and takes a tracker key only from the scope; the replay has no scope, so the developer's answer is the origin's branch.
The mid-flight mode starts from the origin's propose commit; the port ran no propose session.
The plan-lint refusal of the origin's tasks outside every group (D8); see rule unassigned-tasks.

cite.phrase: in a host a flow defect is a defect of the plugin; it is a record of kind `adf` in the core's debt store

rules.why: The origin's flow-debt destination is the port's adf-debt.

cite.phrase: the blocking part is the change's own strict validation (`validateProject` with the change)

rules.why: The origin's check 1 failed on main specs outside the change; the port validates the change itself.
The origin edited the main spec in a verify-phase commit (a prose edit) that the replay does not make: no reply carries it (D5).

cite.phrase: no agent edits the main specs; the script writes them

rules.why: The port's script writes the merged spec in its own layout (no blank line around `## Requirements`, the `# <capability> Specification` title of a new capability); the origin's main specs were written by an agent. The requirements are the same.
verify.md is rendered from the port's template, one section per check id.

cite.phrase: rendered by `assemble`; `review.mjs check` reads it back

rules.why: review.md is rendered by review.mjs assemble: findings numbered F<n>, the suite after the fixes.
The record holds the output of the sandbox's fake suite command, in the port's record format.

cite.phrase: a task ID comes from the tracker scope as a suggestion (`scope.mjs select` names the branch key)

rules.why: The port records the tracker scope of a change (scope.json, the proposal's Scope sources); the origin had no scope step.

cite.phrase: a script ticks a task by its id when the task's dispatch returns

rules.why: The port ticks each task by script when its dispatch returns, one commit each.

cite.phrase: Fan-out within the cap is mandatory

rules.why: The port runs every group in its own worktree and merges it; the origin ran some groups on the change branch (its deviation records say so).

cite.phrase: committed on its own as `chore(metrics): record <name>`

rules.why: The port commits the metrics record on its own after the ingest.

cite.phrase: the message is fixed by the script, `docs(openspec): review <change>`

rules.why: The review record commit has the port's subject.
The origin's fix commit is not in git any more (the branch is gone), so no fix reply exists; the finding was accepted by an injected ruling.

Work the origin committed on the branch after its archive and ingest (merge request review fixes, a merge of the integration branch), outside every flow phase; the port's review stage runs the same review before archive.

Commits the origin made in apply outside any task (the final review's fixes, the sweep's consolidation): the replay replies only task commits, and the final review and the sweep get an injected clean reply.
Commits the driver made to work around a refusal (a split fix).
The driver merges the host setup into the in-flight branch, as the switch brings it to an in-flight change.

The origin's integration branch changed the file between the change's base and its merge, outside the change; the port made the same edit as the origin's change, so the difference is that drift alone: the replay starts from the base (D3).

The records give no ingest reply for this change (no log bullet or paragraph the reply builder reads), so the replay injected nothingLearned or a partial reply; the origin's memory edits are not made.
The knowledge base's log entry carries the replay's time and git identity; the entry is otherwise the origin's.
The difference comes from a step the replay synthesized (a reply, a ruling, a placement or a workaround).
The origin's integration branch moved between the change's base and its merge; the replay starts from the base (D3).
A file the replay's host setup wrote: the edits the switch makes (iteration 15).
The mid-flight mode ends at archive; the developer's merge (land) is not run.
The port's change metadata is .adf.json, not .openspec.yaml.

cite.phrase: The base is snapshotted at propose into the change's `specs-base.json`

rules.why: The port snapshots the delta specs' base at propose for archive's three-way check.

cite.phrase: "performed" is the wave-1 groups a group dispatch name of `attempts.jsonl` carries

rules.why: The port records every dispatch attempt; the metrics read it.
